about: Every source the F/A-18C build draws on (claude/plans/air-fa18c.md). use: trace = may be traced and matched; facts = its facts may be cited, its figures are never traced into the repository; look = looked at only. Photos (dvids*) are of the reference airframe, BuNo 164718, unless their aircraft says otherwise. fetch.py downloads each entry with a url into references/ and checks its hash.

references.authors: DC Designs for Microsoft

references.note: Look only by preference; never traced, fitted, snapped to or copied unless no other way gives the shape a detail needs, when a specified detail may be copied, never the whole model, as fair use (air-fa18c.md #2, amended 2026-11-04); its textures never. Each measurement in facts.json names it as its source with the reason; each copied detail is listed here with what, where and why. The build scripts never open it. aircraft.unit: U.S. Navy Flight Demonstration Squadron (Blue Angels)

references.shows: No. 2 from its left, level with its wings (0-5 deg below), beam on, in formation: the lower outline from radome to stabilator against clear sky; No. 1's fin tip hides its canopy's top.
references.note: For the sky check's coverage (#47): a clean legacy Hornet, with no pylons and only wingtip rails, so its lower outline is not hidden behind store boxes. The Blue Angels' jets carry no gun (its port faired over) and a smoke system; their outline is the fleet F/A-18C's. Blue Angels F/A-18C; bottom jet No. 2, BuNo 163451 (legible on aft fuselage), pilot Lt Damon Kroes; also No. 4 (inverted, top), No. 1 (inverted) and No. 3 in the Double Farvel
